content.user_title: Review Web App Security Before Release
content.value_statement: Security issues often appear when teams add authentication, APIs, payments, uploads, or sensitive data flows. This skill provides a focused checklist and review prompts for finding common web application risks before deployment.
actual_capabilities: Reviews secrets management practices, including environment variables, hardcoded keys, logs, and git history checks.
Checks input validation, file upload rules, SQL injection controls, and XSS protections.
Guides authentication, authorization, CSRF, session cookie, and row level security reviews.
Includes pre-deployment checks for security headers, CORS, HTTPS, dependencies, and rate limiting.
Provides security testing examples for authentication, authorization, input validation, and rate limiting.
Covers Solana wallet and transaction verification for blockchain-related changes.
limitations: It is a checklist and guidance resource; it does not run scanners or inspect code automatically.
It focuses on common web application risks and may not cover every framework or compliance requirement.
It cannot prove production configuration is correct without access to deployed settings and logs.
Blockchain guidance is limited to basic Solana wallet and transaction verification patterns.

use_cases.title: Review an API endpoint before deployment
use_cases.description: Check validation, authorization, rate limits, error handling, and sensitive data exposure before a new endpoint reaches production.

use_cases.title: Standardize pull request security checks
use_cases.description: Apply the same checklist across code reviews for authentication, secrets, dependency updates, and unsafe logging.

use_cases.title: Prepare a sensitive feature for launch
use_cases.description: Review payments, uploads, user data, and third-party API integrations before accepting real customer traffic.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Security Checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review for a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change for hardcoded secrets, input validation, authentication, authorization, and unsafe logging. Summarize the highest risks first.

prompt_templates.title: Review a New API Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this new API endpoint for validation, authorization, CSRF risk, rate limiting, error messages, and sensitive data exposure.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Sensitive Data Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review for secrets or user data
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace this sensitive data flow from input to storage and logs. Identify risks in secrets handling, access control, errors, and third-party calls.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Release Security Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a release security review plan for this feature. Cover tests, security headers, row level security, rate limits, dependencies, and remediation order.

output_examples.input: A new user profile endpoint accepts email, display name, and avatar upload.
output: High priority: require authentication and verify users can only update their own profile.
Medium priority: validate file size, MIME type, and extension for avatar uploads.
Medium priority: return generic validation errors and avoid exposing internal storage paths.

output_examples.input: A checkout flow stores a payment provider token and returns error details to the browser.
output: High priority: ensure payment tokens are never logged or stored outside the approved provider flow.
High priority: replace detailed payment errors shown to users with safe generic messages.
Medium priority: add rate limiting and monitoring for repeated checkout attempts.

output_examples.input: A Supabase admin feature reads user records and updates roles.
output: High priority: verify server-side admin authorization before every role update.
High priority: confirm row level security policies block normal users from reading other accounts.
Medium priority: add audit logging that records actor, target user, and action without secrets.

best_practices: Review risky changes before implementation and again before deployment.
Require evidence for each checklist item, such as tests, headers, policies, or configuration screenshots.
Prioritize fixes that protect secrets, user data, payments, and authorization boundaries.
anti_patterns: Treating checklist completion as proof of safety without inspecting the actual code path.
Reviewing only frontend controls while backend authorization remains unverified.
Ignoring logs, error messages, and deployment settings during security review.

faq.question: Does this skill replace a professional penetration test?
faq.answer: No. It helps structure review work, but high-risk systems still need specialist testing and production verification.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that support skill-based guidance.

faq.question: What types of applications does it fit best?
faq.answer: It fits web applications with authentication, APIs, file uploads, payments, secrets, user data, or Supabase integration.

faq.question: Does it automatically scan my repository?
faq.answer: No. It provides review structure and prompts. You still need to supply code context and verify findings.

faq.question: How should teams use it in pull requests?
faq.answer: Run the checklist on risky changes, record evidence for each item, and block release until high-risk issues are resolved.

faq.question: Does it cover blockchain security?
faq.answer: It includes basic Solana wallet and transaction checks, but it does not cover full smart contract audits.
